text:
samira_supp: Heads-up — CSM Rachel reported a month-end reconciliation mismatch for acct ZetaHealth. Invoice #INV-98321 shows line item 'Pro Plus' $12,000 but our dashboard snapshot shows tokens billed under 'Pro' and totals ~ $7,200. Customer caught this during their month-close.
rachel_csm: They attached the invoice PDF and the CSV export from the dashboard. Customer says they expected a downgrade to Pro on 2025-12-15; invoice still shows Pro Plus. Sharing artifacts now.
samira_supp: Links: invoice PDF <https://invoices.redwood/INV-98321>, dashboard snapshot <https://dash.redwood/zetahealth/reports/2025-12-31>. Quick note: dashboard token sum = 1,200,450; invoice token line = 2,400,900 (exactly 2x). That smells like duplicated aggregation.
jordan_billing: @samira_supp can you paste the raw usage rollup query and any metering/rollup job logs you have? Exact doubling usually means the rollup ran twice or a join duplicated rows during invoice line creation.
samira_supp: Raw rollup I used to sanity-check:
```sql
-- usage rollup
SELECT account_id, day, SUM(tokens) AS tokens
FROM usage_events
WHERE account_id = 'acct_zeta' AND day BETWEEN '2025-12-01' AND '2025-12-31'
GROUP BY account_id, day;
```
Also grepped the job logs for meter/rollup runs.
dev-billing-bot: metering-run completed for cutoff=2025-12-31 job_id=mr-20251231-42 status=success duration=00:05:12
jordan_billing: Bot shows the primary run succeeded. Can you check if the post-proration/backfill job `prorate_and_rollup` re-ran after the main metering? We had a hotfix that could have requeued retries around the cutoff.
michael_fin: If invoice tokens are an exact multiple, check whether proration rows were applied both before and after rollup (double-applied proration). That would inflate invoice token counts and push the line into the higher plan tier.
samira_supp: I searched logs: `prorate_and_rollup` executed at 2025-12-31T23:58:14Z and again at 2026-01-01T00:02:09Z. The second run has different run_id but same cutoff window.
jordan_billing: Confirmed — the second run looks like a retry path that re-inserted prorated invoice_lines without dedupe. I can reproduce locally by replaying those two runs and seeing doubled invoice_lines.
jordan_billing: Short-term mitigation: I'll add an idempotency guard on invoice_lines insert to skip rows where (run_id, cutoff) already exists. Deploying patch to staging now.
jordan_billing: Planned backfill SQL (will run after patch):
```sql
INSERT INTO invoice_lines (account_id, cutoff, run_id, tokens, amount, description)
SELECT rt.account_id, rt.cutoff, rt.run_id, rt.tokens, rt.amount, rt.desc
FROM rollup_tmp rt
LEFT JOIN invoice_lines il ON il.account_id = rt.account_id AND il.cutoff = rt.cutoff AND il.description = rt.desc
WHERE il.account_id IS NULL;
```
samira_supp: Thanks. I'll inform Rachel and the customer that we identified a duplicate rollup path and will issue a corrected invoice + credit once backfill completes.
rachel_csm: Customer asked for ETA — can we commit to a window?
jordan_billing: Patch + backfill tonight — estimate within 6 hours. Will post backfill run_id and verification summary here when done.
samira_supp: :thumbsup: please also add a short note in the ticket about the customer-facing messaging so support can send the corrected PDF and credit note.
dev-billing-bot: ticket created BLG-4218 assigned_to=jordan_billing severity=high
michael_fin: Finance will approve the credit after we validate the corrected invoice. Please include before/after token totals and checksum.
jordan_billing: Will do. I'll drop the run artifacts and a simple diff of invoice_lines here after backfill.
samira_supp: I'll close the loop with the customer once we have the corrected invoice. Thanks everyone.
